our_title: CMake libScotch lacks five Makefile-built sources, so SCOTCH_contextBindMesh and three Fortran wrappers are missing
ran: CMake 3.28.3, CI flags (-DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo -DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON), trees $WORK/cm/{base32 = copy of v7.0.18, patched32, patched64 (-DINTSIZE=64)}. `nm -D base32/lib/libscotch.so | grep -cE ' T (SCOTCH_contextBindMesh|SCOTCHFCONTEXTBINDMESH|scotchfgraphinducelist_|scotchfgraphinducepart_|scotchfnumsizeof_|_SCOTCHhgraphDump)$'` -> 0/6 (Makefile build $INFRA/asan has them); patched32 -> 6/6. `sh ci/check_sources.sh <v7.0.18>/src` -> `< hgraph_dump.c < library_context_mesh.c < library_context_mesh_f.c < library_graph_induce_f.c < library_memory_f.c > common_error.c` and `> symbol_fax.c` (libesmumps), rc=1; on the series rc=0.
severity_note: Same as the review: a public routine declared in scotch.h (SCOTCH_contextBindMesh) and documented Fortran wrappers cannot be linked from a CMake-built library, which is what distributions and CI use.
evidence: src/libscotch/CMakeLists.txt:267-268 'hgraph_check.c / hgraph_induce.c' (no hgraph_dump.c); :357 'library_context_f.c' (no library_context_mesh*.c); :376-377 'library_graph_f.c / library_graph_io_chac.c' (no library_graph_induce_f.c); :399 'library_memory.c' (no library_memory_f.c); :199/:201 'bgraph_cost.c' twice; :243 'library_graph_induce.c' out of place.
review_accuracy: Accurate on the five files and the consequence. Imprecise on which 'memory' wrapper is lost: library_memory_f.c provides scotchfnumsizeof (SCOTCH_numSizeof), not the memory statistics wrappers (scotchfmemcur/scotchfmemmax live in library_common_f.c, which CMake builds). hgraph_dump.c is an internal debugging helper with no public caller, so its absence only matters for consistency.
first_pass_critique: Status and location right, but the nm evidence is wrong: it cites 'scotchfmemcur' as the symbol of library_memory_f.c, whereas that file defines scotchfnumsizeof (the CMake build has scotchfmemcur from library_common_f.c). It did not run cmake (a working cmake wheel was in the uv cache). It missed that the same list also carries a dead file (common_error.c) that leaks un-prefixed symbols, and the libesmumps mismatch (symbol_fax.c), both found by the very CI check it proposed. Its 'single-source' option 3 is dismissed as 'unlikely to be accepted' without trying it; a working configure-time version exists (alt c).

fix_options.summary: Add the five .c files and hgraph_dump.h at their alphabetical place, drop the duplicate bgraph_cost.c, move library_graph_induce.c to its place; separate commits remove the dead common_error.c and the standalone symbol_fax.c; a checker script and the Makefile rule typos are separate commits.

our_title: Installed SCOTCHConfig.cmake includes EsMUMPS target files that suffixed builds never install
ran: $WORK/cm/suffix.sh: pristine v7.0.18 with -DSCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX=_pys -DENABLE_TESTS=OFF, make install, consumer project repro/BLD-02/consumer: `CMake Error at .../inst-suffix-base/lib/cmake/scotch/SCOTCHConfig.cmake:111 (include)` and `:114 (include)` (no esmumpsTargets.cmake installed), rc=1. Patched: configure prints 'EsMUMPS library not built because SCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX is set', consumer configures (SCOTCH_FOUND=1, SCOTCH_LIBESMUMPS_FOUND empty), builds and prints 'no scotch-internal macros in consumer'.
severity_note: Lower than the review's High: only installs configured with SCOTCH_NAME_SUFFIX are affected (CI never builds one, BLD-14), but for those every find_package(SCOTCH) is a hard error.
evidence: src/CMakeLists.txt:224 'if(BUILD_LIBESMUMPS AND NOT USE_SUFFIX)' / :225 'add_subdirectory(esmumps)'; cmake/SCOTCHConfig.cmake.in:85 'if(@BUILD_LIBESMUMPS@)' / :87 'include("${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/esmumpsTargets.cmake")' / :90 'include("${CMAKE_CURRENT_LIST_DIR}/ptesmumpsTargets.cmake")'; CMakeLists.txt:99 'option(BUILD_LIBESMUMPS "Build EsMUMPS library" ON)' is never changed when USE_SUFFIX is set (:86-88).
review_accuracy: Accurate; its first fix ('@BUILD_LIBESMUMPS@ AND NOT @USE_SUFFIX@') would work but leaves BUILD_LIBESMUMPS lying about what is built, and USE_SUFFIX is unset (not OFF) without a suffix, which configure_package_config_file would substitute as an empty string: 'if(ON AND NOT )' is a syntax error. The OPTIONAL variant hides the problem and leaves SCOTCH_LIBESMUMPS_FOUND=ON (verified at runtime, alt b).
first_pass_critique: Correct status and the right idea (one effective value), but source-read only although cmake was available; its preferred patch adds a second variable (BUILD_LIBESMUMPS_EFFECTIVE) instead of fixing BUILD_LIBESMUMPS itself where USE_SUFFIX is decided, and its sketch sets the variable in src/ after the fact. Its remark that the review's fix 'applies to ptesmumps implicitly' is right.

our_title: Both MeTiS libraries carry the metis.h generation rule; parallel make runs dummysizes twice on it
ran: base32 (pristine 7.0.18): rule copies: 'Generate scotch.h' in 8 build.make files (dummysizes, ptdummysizes, scotch, scotcherr, scotcherrexit, ptscotch, ptscotcherr, ptscotcherrexit), 'Generating metis.h' and 'Generating metisf.h' in scotchmetisv3 and scotchmetisv5, 'Copy esmumps.h' in esmumps and ptesmumps. Race loop, 10 x (rm the generated header; make -j3): metis.h generated 2 times in 10/10 runs, metisf.h 2 times in 4/10 (cm/race-base-all.log), esmumps.h 2 times in 6/10 (cm/race-base-esmumps.log). 3 clean pristine builds (configure + make -j3, cm/suffix.out): every header, scotch.h and ptscotch.h included, generated once (the race needs both libraries to be scheduled together, as in the incremental loop), because every other owner depends on dummysizes. Patched32: 10 x -> 1/1/1 (cm/race-patched-all.log).
severity_note: As the review: nondeterministic parallel build in CI (make -j16); two dummysizes processes rewrite the same header while the other library may be compiling against it. No corrupted header observed in 10 runs, but nothing prevents it.
evidence: libscotchmetis/CMakeLists.txt:84-85 '${GENERATED_INCLUDE_DIR}/metis.h / ${GENERATED_INCLUDE_DIR}/metisf.h)' in add_library(scotchmetisv${version} ...) for version 3 and 5, no add_dependencies left; esmumps/CMakeLists.txt:91 '${GENERATED_INCLUDE_DIR}/esmumps.h)' in esmumps_headers, used by add_library(esmumps ...) :93 and add_library(ptesmumps ...) :141.
upstream_change: 635741dd Bugfix: enable parallel build with older Bison versions [report A. Lindsay]: removes every *_h / parser_*_c custom target and lists the generated files as target sources instead

upstream_fix_review.details: Right for its own report: parser_yy.c/parser_ly.h/parser_ll.c are now produced by the scotch target only (src/libscotch/CMakeLists.txt:107-140; one build.make holds the Bison rule), and scotch.h/ptscotch.h are safe because dummysizes/ptdummysizes list them (:52,:55) and every other owner depends on (pt)dummysizes through 'DEPENDS dummysizes' (3 clean -j3 builds: one 'Generate scotch.h' each). But the same removal left two independent owners for metis.h/metisf.h (libscotchmetis/CMakeLists.txt:84-85, foreach 3 5) and esmumps.h (esmumps/CMakeLists.txt:91,93,141), against the add_custom_command rule that an output used by several targets must be driven by one custom target: metis.h is generated twice in 10/10 parallel runs, and metisf.h, which 7.0.17 serialized through metisf_h, now twice in 4/10 (new: PS3-G29-1). Not a build failure in 20 runs here (dummysizes writes a few KB), but two writers on one file can leave a truncated header to a concurrent compiler.
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Our 7.0.17 commit added the missing metis_h dependency next to the existing metisf_h; that context no longer exists. Rewritten for 7.0.18: one custom target per directory (metis_h for both MeTiS headers, esmumps_h) that both libraries of each pair depend on; it keeps his removal of the parser and scotch.h targets. His version is better for the parser and scotch.h (fewer targets); ours is needed for the two pairs.

review_accuracy: Accurate; the Makefile-generator mechanism is exactly what the generated build.make files show. Its fix line mentions parmetis_h, which is only a consistency fix (one consumer), and 'drop the generated header from per-target sources', which is optional once the dependency exists.
first_pass_critique: Right status and preferred option, and right that parmetis.h is not racy. Source-read although it could have run the Makefile generator; its note that option 2 'needs GENERATED set' is moot (the property is already set at :53). Missed the .NOTPARALLEL trap, which makes a naive reproduction report 'no race'.

extra_instances.quote: add_custom_command(OUTPUT ${GENERATED_INCLUDE_DIR}/metisf.h ... ; ${GENERATED_INCLUDE_DIR}/metisf.h) in both MeTiS libraries (metisf_h target removed by 635741dd)
